increments.title: A correction round of pure coverage gaps runs test-author and reviewer only
increments.goal: Let the reviewer classify each finding it returns as a coverage gap or a defect, and have the workflow run a round whose findings are all coverage gaps through test-author and reviewer alone, visibly and on the record.
criteria: The reviewer's structured return carries a per-finding classification field that says whether the finding is a coverage gap or a defect; it is a value the reviewer sets, not a phrase the workflow greps out of prose.
When every finding of a round is classified a coverage gap, that correction round runs the test-author and the reviewer only, and does not run the researcher or the implementer.
A round with at least one finding classified a defect runs the full four-agent chain exactly as it does today.
The workflow log()s that it is correcting coverage only when it takes the shortened path.
The reviewer's classification of each finding is recorded in backlog.json alongside the round it belongs to.
The reviewer's own brief states what makes a finding a coverage gap rather than a defect, so the classification is decided the same way twice.
The test suite passes.
increments.note: Accepted at review round 2 with no findings: the per-finding kind enum, the coverage-only routing in both workflows, the log line, the recorded classification and the reviewer's stated rule are all pinned by test-repo.sh drivers w17/w18/w19 and a backlog recorder case; bash test-repo.sh 71 cases exit 0 and ./test.sh all 6 suites exit 0.

increments.title: The UI test harness returns null for an id the rendered markup does not contain
increments.goal: Stop the argus-ui test harness conjuring an element for every id, so an assertion that reads a container the page never rendered fails the way a browser would, and prove the harness with a case in the suite.
criteria: installFakes in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs resolves an id the rendered markup does not contain to null rather than to a created-and-cached fake element.

Every existing case in the suite still passes, or is corrected to assert what the page actually renders; the report says which cases were corrected and why each was passing against markup the page never wrote.

A case in the suite proves the harness itself: it removes a container from the rendered markup and shows at least one assertion going red as a result, so the guard is part of the run rather than a manual mutation check.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test passes, with the case count reported.

increments.title: parse-agent-log reports a whole workflow run
increments.goal: Give bin/parse-agent-log a mode that takes a workflow run directory and reports the run as one thing, and point the retro skill at that mode instead of at a hand-run loop.
criteria: bin/parse-agent-log accepts a workflow run directory and reports the run as a single report rather than one transcript at a time.
That report carries per-agent-type totals, per-agent rows in the journal's order, a tool breakdown that shows failures, and which agents started without returning.
The existing single-transcript behaviour of the tool still works.
The retro skill's instructions tell the session to use the run-directory mode and no longer tell it to loop the tool over each transcript and re-join the results by hand.

No page left in the repository still describes the tool as transcript-at-a-time only or still asks a reader to re-join results by hand; the report names each page that documents the tool and says whether it needed correcting.
The new mode has test coverage that goes red when the report drops a section or miscounts, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: Added the stale-page criterion: two of this increment's three review rounds spent themselves on pages that described the old chain after the behaviour changed, so an increment that changes documented behaviour now has to account for every page that documents it.

increments.title: backlog.mjs record takes the step return on stdin
increments.goal: Let the recorder read a step return from stdin as well as from a file path, and instruct agents to use the stdin form, so no agent has to survive a heredoc to record a summary containing quotes or markup.
criteria: backlog.mjs record accepts the step return on stdin as well as from a file path, and a return containing quotes, HTML attributes and newlines records correctly through the stdin form.
The file-path form of backlog.mjs record keeps working unchanged.
The agent brief instructs agents to record their step return through the stdin form.
Every other page that tells an agent how to record a step return says the same thing as the brief; the report names each page checked and each corrected.
The change has test coverage that goes red when the stdin form breaks or when the file-path form regresses, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: Split: the collector fixture left this increment for collector-fixture, because the two share only a mention in the agent brief and a finding against either would otherwise force a full correction round on both. Added the stale-page criterion for the same reason as run-report — the record instruction is repeated outside the brief.

increments.title: An agent that needs a live collector has a documented way to start and stop one
increments.goal: Make starting and stopping a collector for ad-hoc inspection a documented, reachable thing rather than something an agent improvises with a pkill, and name it where agents will find it.
criteria: A documented way to start and stop a collector for ad-hoc inspection exists — a script or an existing test helper made reachable.
Starting and then stopping it leaves no process holding the port, and the report shows that checked.
The agent brief names that way, so an agent needing a live instance is told what to run instead of improvising a pkill.
The change has test coverage that goes red when start or stop breaks, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: New, split off agent-affordances: it is a process-lifecycle deliverable in the collector's own tooling, it fails for reasons the recorder change cannot cause, and closing one while the other is blocked is worth the separate chain.

increments.title: test.sh catches a commit-signing misconfiguration before an agent commits
increments.goal: Make ./test.sh verify that commit signing actually works in the environment it runs in, so a signing failure surfaces before an agent's first commit rather than after its work is done.
criteria: ./test.sh verifies that commit signing works in the environment it runs in — a signed commit in a throwaway repository, or the equivalent check the setup allows.
The check fails loudly and says what is misconfigured when signing does not work, and leaves nothing behind in the repository under test.
The check does not make ./test.sh fail in an environment where signing is legitimately not configured for the run, and the report states which behaviour was chosen and why.
./test.sh is green, and the report names the command, what it covered and its exit code.

increments.title: The loop skill pages tell the session how to tell a dead run from a live one
increments.goal: Correct the loop skill pages so the invoking session establishes liveness from the task's own status and knows that a user turn kills a running workflow.
criteria: The loop skill pages tell the invoking session to establish whether the run is alive from the task's own status, and say plainly that transcript file timestamps do not establish it.
The pages say that an ordinary user turn kills a running workflow, and that the killed agent restarts from zero rather than resuming mid-flight, so an interruption costs a whole agent.
The pages tell a session that takes a message mid-run to check liveness and resume rather than to report progress from stale files.
The pages do not describe the periodic self check-in or the resumeFromRunId re-entry, which another issue owns.
No loop skill page is left saying something the coverage-only correction round made false, such as an enumeration of the agents a correction round runs; the report names each page checked.
increments.note: Added the last criterion: the coverage-only round changed which agents a correction round runs, and this increment is the run's last pass over the loop pages, so it is where a page left stale by that change gets caught.

return.summary: Closed coverage-only-round as done: the review accepted it with no findings after two correction rounds, both of them stale-prose defects rather than coverage gaps. Re-cut the six remaining increments against that. One split: agent-affordances bundled the recorder's stdin form with the collector start/stop fixture, and this increment showed what a bundle costs — a single finding on one half forces a full four-agent round on the whole increment, and those two halves share nothing but a mention in the agent brief. The recorder keeps the id agent-affordances; the collector fixture is the new collector-fixture and follows it, since neither blocks the other. One sharpening, applied to run-report, agent-affordances and liveness-docs: both correction rounds of coverage-only-round were spent on pages that still described the behaviour the change had just replaced (the README twice, the test-author's page, the reviewer's own enumeration), so every increment that changes a documented contract now carries a criterion that no page is left stale and that the report names the pages it checked. ui-harness-null and signing-check are unchanged: nothing this increment showed touches them, and churn there would cost a reader the ability to see what moved. Order is unchanged otherwise, risk first: ui-harness-null next, because correcting installFakes may turn an unknown number of the suite's 234 cases red and that is the run's biggest unknown; then run-report, the largest new build; then the two affordances; then signing-check; then liveness-docs, pure prose and cheapest, which is also where a loop page left stale by the coverage-only round gets caught. Issue criteria map one-to-one: coverage routing and its visibility to coverage-only-round (done); installFakes returning null and the harness proof case to ui-harness-null; parse-agent-log's run mode and the retro skill to run-report; record-on-stdin and the brief instruction to agent-affordances; the documented collector start/stop and its mention in the brief to collector-fixture; the signing check and 'test.sh is green' to signing-check; the loop-page liveness correction to liveness-docs. Two observations the reviewer explicitly said need no round — the test-author page's frontmatter description still ending 'its caller runs the implementer next', and a ragged wrap at README.md line 79 — are left unraised rather than turned into work nobody asked for.
